title: Lakehouse: iceberg-pg PG-ssl cert-rotate (standby-first, replication intact)
description: cert-rotate on the lakehouse tier now ALSO rotates the Iceberg catalog-DB pair iceberg-pg (GAP #6, v0.8.8)  --  previously a graceful skip. Shares PgSslCertRotator with grafana-pg: rotates the PG17 streaming pair STANDBY-FIRST then PRIMARY via a vault-agent re-issue + a SIGHUP `systemctl reload postgresql@17-main` (NOT a restart), so the streaming-replication connection AND Nessie's live catalog connections are never dropped. Live-verified 2026-07-07 on the clean 1-primary + 1-standby pair.

prerequisites.smokeGate: iceberg-pg pair on the current Vault root (vault-agents active); 1 primary + 1 streaming standby (nexus health lakehouse -> iceberg-pg-replication green)

steps.command: ssh -i $NEXUS_SSH_KEY nexusadmin@192.168.70.149 "sudo -u postgres psql -tAc 'SELECT pg_is_in_recovery()'; sudo -u postgres psql -tAc \"SELECT client_addr,state FROM pg_stat_replication\""

observe.what: iceberg-pg-1 (.149) is the primary (in_recovery=f) and sees the standby streaming (192.168.10.150 | streaming). This is the pre-rotation baseline.

the per-node old/new serial table: iceberg-pg-2 (standby) rotates BEFORE iceberg-pg-1 (primary); both show a fresh newSerial. (MinIO/Nessie rows also rotate; Spark/ZooKeeper are graceful N/A  --  no rotatable leaf.)

observe.where: ssh nexusadmin@192.168.70.149 'sudo -u postgres psql -tAc "SELECT client_addr,state FROM pg_stat_replication"'
observe.what: AFTER the rotation the primary STILL shows 192.168.10.150 | streaming  --  the SIGHUP reload did not drop the replication connection

whatProves: iceberg-pg TLS-leaf rotation is a real, in-CLI operation (not a DR-runbook deferral): both nodes of the Iceberg catalog DB get fresh certs, standby-first, and PostgreSQL streaming replication survives because PG re-reads the leaf via a SIGHUP reload instead of a restart. Nessie's catalog front door keeps working throughout.
